answer: Like a harbor charging docking ships, this entry tax charges each identity. A newcomer files an entry signed with a quill. Its receipt is sealed with jade binding payment to that identity. The tax is 25 POA, burned at entry, so the k-th fake identity still costs a fresh 25 POA: 1,000 fakes sink 25,000 POA, nothing recoverable. An honest agent pays once and keeps its full share; a forger buying in bulk only multiplies its own sunk cost. The named failure is payment rental, one payer funding many entries; it fails because each entry matches one payment, and reuse is rejected.
